limits: Collection disabled, physical freeing enabled. manual_review.connection_release: g_conn_release at 0x21cc0 uses 40 frame bytes excluding incoming return address. It decrements the transport count, unregisters/closes the descriptor and releases TLS and in/out buffers, then returns at 0x21dcf without freeing the connection record.
manual_review.task_release: fwp_free_zombie at 0xcd30 saves one 8-byte register. After removing stack and GC links it checks counted at 0xcde0; client I/O tasks have zero there and jump to return, bypassing task-object release.

hosts.scope:
One native client process makes 1, 16 or 256 batches of remote calls over loopback HTTP/2 to an interpreted greeter. Each response contains integers 1..64. Full batches sum all 64; partial batches sum only the first 32; retained batches sum an initial stream, make and sum a second call while retaining the initial iterator, then reread its first value. Retained batches therefore make twice as many calls. Raw unoptimized interpreter and ordinary native output must agree. Three separate instrumented processes per case count managed allocations/retains/charged bytes, created/finalized connection and stream objects, and requested/freed queued-message bytes including their header and trailing byte. GC is disabled, physical freeing enabled. Counters start after constant initialization. Final counters follow root execution, joining its child tasks and cached-value cleanup, before whole-runtime shutdown. Before the final sample, measurement hooks close every pooled connection and drain all detached I/O tasks. Checkpoints are immediately before each new stream is allocated, after connection selection and request-header preparation; a checkpoint can deliberately include an earlier retained iterator. Excludes other raw buffers, TLS/OS/allocator metadata, server/whole-process memory and timing. Native builds use ordinary -O2. Source, generated C, executables and raw stderr are retained.

Connection-churn variant: measurement-only native hooks close the pool before each new call and after cached-value cleanup, cancel/wait for the detached connection reader and writer, and require zero live I/O tasks and one closed socket per created connection before sampling. Each call uses a new connection. Ordinary native and interpreter executions still use their usual pooling: their output is the functional reference, not an equivalent transport workload. Compare ownership revisions using these same churn hooks; do not use this experiment as a timing comparison with pooled calls. Retained iterators still keep earlier cached values across connection closure. Drain rows record created/closed connections, live I/O tasks, managed charge, unfinalized connection/request counts and unread message bytes. Scheduler stack pools, other raw buffers and TLS/OS storage remain excluded.

binary_observations.limits: Static inspection only. No downloaded executable ran. Symbols inlined by the compiler can be absent; the typed cache destructor must be present. Disassembly requires human review for loops, frame sizes and register use. No timing claim.

manual_review.connection_release: g_conn_release at 0x1e130 reserves 48 frame bytes including saved registers. It decrements the transport count, unregisters/closes the descriptor and releases TLS and in/out buffers, then returns at 0x1e224 without freeing the connection record.
manual_review.task_release: fwp_free_zombie at 0xbb48 reserves 32 bytes including saved registers. After stack and GC-link removal it loads counted at 0xbbe0; client I/O tasks have zero there and branch at 0xbbec to return, bypassing task-object release.
